message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (Room Temp)** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (−423.2 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (−434.6 °F) |
| | Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound in H₂ | ~1275 m s⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Behavior** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) with a single covalent bond |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Acidic strength | Very weak acid (pKa ≈ 35) |
| | Basicity | Very weak base (pKb ≈ 35) |
| | Reactivity | Highly flammable; reacts with O₂, N₂, halogens, metals, and many organic compounds |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (≈0.0006 M) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Good in nonpolar solvents (e.g., hexane, benzene) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant (~99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 0.015 % natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion research |
| | Chemical differences | Deuterium forms stronger bonds (bond dissociation energy ≈ 443 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Physical differences | Deuterium gas is heavier (density ≈ 0.180 g L⁻¹) |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel cell technology | Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity via H₂ + O₂ → H₂O |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) + liquid oxygen (LOX) |
| | Chemical industry | Production of ammonia (NH₃), methanol (CH₃OH), and other hydrogenated products |
| | Metallurgy | Hydrogen embrittlement mitigation, hydrogen annealing |
| | Medical imaging | Deuterium-labeled compounds in NMR/MRI |
| | Nuclear fusion | Deuterium–tritium fusion (D-T) in experimental reactors |
| | Food industry | Hydrogenation of oils, deuterated solvents for analytical chemistry |
| **Astrophysical & Environmental Role** | Stellar fusion | Proton–proton chain (p + p → d + e⁺ + ν_e) powers main‑sequence stars |
| | Big Bang nucleosynthesis | First element formed after the Big Bang |
| | Greenhouse effect | Hydrogen itself is not a greenhouse gas, but its combustion releases water vapor, a potent greenhouse gas |
| | Air composition | ~0.000055 % by volume in Earth's atmosphere |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability range (air) | 4 % – 75 % (by volume) |
| | Explosion limits | Lower explosive limit (LEL) ≈ 4 %, upper explosive limit (UEL) ≈ 75 % |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic, but can cause asphyxiation by displacing oxygen |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders or cryogenic tanks; special safety protocols for handling LH₂ |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, consisting of one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds, from simple diatomic H₂ to complex organometallics.
- **Energy carrier**: Central to fuel cell technology and rocket propulsion.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Deuterium and tritium provide unique chemical and physical properties useful in research and industry.
- **Astrophysical importance**: The building block of stars and the universe’s first element.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
